nodes.title: llama.cpp · Quick setup
widgets_values:
## llama.cpp · Quick setup
1. Install [ComfyUI-llama-multimodal](https://github.com/craftingmod/ComfyUI-llama-multimodal) separately; follow its runtime/GPU setup instructions.
2. Download compatible GGUF models (e.g. [mradermacher on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/models)). Put them in `ComfyUI/models/LLM/` or a configured LLM path. Refresh/restart.
3. **Gen #1 (vision):** select the GGUF and its matching `mmproj` in Create Native Session. Start with `n_ctx=8192`; increase only if the complete request needs more context and fits in memory.
4. **Gen #2 (text):** select its own GGUF in Create Native Session; `mmproj=[none]`. Choose the correct model profile for EACH pass (e.g. Gemma 4 vs Qwen non-thinking). Use non-thinking where supported for clean Director outputs.
5. **Prefill:** separate profiles; start with `n_batch=1024`, reduce to 512 if needed. Leave image token limits and `n_ubatch` at 0 (automatic/default); Director already scales vision inputs. Hardware profile: adjust GPU layers and KV cache to your available memory, not just GGUF size.

[llama.cpp multimodal documentation](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/mtmd/README.md) · [Nodepack setup & troubleshooting](https://github.com/craftingmod/ComfyUI-llama-multimodal)

Model, quantization, context, image count and GPU memory all matter. Start conservatively; these are starting points, not universal requirements.

**Native Sessions:** install the supported multimodal llama-cpp-python fork in ComfyUI’s environment (see nodepack instructions). Keep `session_unload` enabled on both Generate nodes.
